newsitem.title: USA: Ohio corn seedings edge ahead of year ago/average.
newsitem.headline: Ohio corn seedings edge ahead of year ago/average.

text.p: Ohio corn seedings remained slow due to damp and cool soil conditions, but the pace edged ahead of the year ago and average level during the week ended Sunday, according to the Ohio Agricultural Statistics Service.
Corn seedings as of Sunday stood at six percent complete, above the two percent pace of a year ago and the three percent average pace.
Twelve percent of the winter wheat crop was jointed, above nine percent a year ago and the seven percent average.

The wheat crop was rated three percent very poor, 12 percent poor, 39 percent fair, 37 percent good and nine percent excellent. A week ago four percent of the crop was rated very poor, 13 percent poor, 33 percent fair, 41 percent good and nine percent excellent.
Pasture conditions were one percent very poor, nine percent poor, 36 percent fair, 48 percent good and six percent excellent.
Topsoil moisture levels were rated 22 percent surplus, 76 percent adequate and two percent short.
